title: Navigation API: Marking promises as handled is a poor developer experience

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#255 — filed by @jakearchibald (2022-12). 4 comments, with concrete proposals at the end that @domenic engaged with.

---

### The complaint

> I'll write some code, and because I'm a 0.5x developer I make mistakes. The result won't behave as I'm expecting, so I'll open the console, and there's no error, leading me to think the problem isn't just due to an error being thrown. However, it *is* due to an error being thrown, but the navigation API is swallowing the error.

Errors vanishing from the console is a genuinely costly debugging experience, and it catches out even people who know the API well.

### Why it's not trivially fixable

@domenic's counter-cases — the API can't simply stop marking promises as handled, because plenty of legitimate code ignores `finished`:

```js
await navigation.navigate("/foo").committed;      // doesn't care about finished

navigation.navigate("/foo");
navigation.navigate("/bar");   // aborts /foo's finished promise. Do you care?

navigation.navigate("/foo");
handleTransitionResult(navigation.transition.finished);
```

### Proposals from the thread (unresolved)

- **Special-case `AbortError` `DOMException`s** — only auto-mark those as handled, so genuine exceptions still surface. @jakearchibald: *"I think that's a good idea, and might be useful in other cases too."*
- Have `navigateErrorEvent.preventDefault()` mark the associated promises as fully handled, giving apps an explicit opt-in.

Neither was pursued. Migrating because the DX problem is real, recurring, and there's a concrete narrower fix on the table.

cc @jakearchibald @domenic
